messages:
maria: Heads up — planning a rolling maintenance window in eu-west3 tomorrow 02:00–05:00 UTC. We'll do staggered node drains + NVMe firmware updates on two GPU cohorts. No explicit API downtime expected but you may see short spikes in queueing and cold KV-cache misses. @devon @sam please review the schedule.

devon: Which pools exactly? how much capacity will we take out at peak?

maria: Targets: eu-west3-gpu-a and eu-west3-gpu-b. Drains in batches of 3 nodes (NVIDIA A100/80GB) per cohort. Total impact ~48 GPUs (~12% region capacity) for up to 10m per cohort while reboots complete and caches warm. Backfill policy will pull non-latency critical jobs to us-west2.

sam: We'll need a canary first. Suggest run 1-node drain on pool-b, validate p99/99.9 for 20m, then continue. Also route policy update to prefer-region with fallback to us-west2.

maria: Agreed. Canary on pool-b node-211 first. If p99 increases >200ms or error rate +0.5% we abort. Rollback = uncordon + cancel patch job.

chris: Support/CS wants copy for Dedicated customers w/ reserved capacity. Can you include expected capacity loss and mitigation?

maria: Draft blurb: "We will perform rolling maintenance in eu-west3 on <date>. A subset of GPU hosts will be drained for a firmware update; most customers will see no interruption. Teams with reserved Dedicated pools may see short capacity degradation for up to 10m per cohort while we shift workloads. We will fallback to alternate regions for non-latency traffic. Contact support if you need to schedule an exempted window." Thoughts?

priya: Quick cost note — cross-region backfill to us-west2 will increase egress by ~1.2TB across the window; estimate ~$180 in one-off egress for the operation (charged to infra ops budget). Flagging because last quarter ops bump was larger than expected.

devon: Ops checklist:
```
- run canary drain node-211 (pool-b)
- run perf-check script: scripts/perf/validate_tail.sh --window 20m
- watch trace sampling + console p99 dashboards
- if anomalies: uncordon node, re-run health checks
```

maria: Also enabling prefix + KV cache warmup before each cohort: pseudo command below to prefill keys for common prompts
```
# warmup helper (runs on controller)
./warmup_kvcache --pool eu-west3-gpu-a --prefix-file warm_prefixes.txt --concurrency 12
```

infra-bot: scheduled: maintenance window queued for 2026-03-21T02:00Z -> 2026-03-21T05:00Z (id: mw-eu3-20260321). Canaries: node-211. Notifying oncall.

sam: One more: update routing rules to add short TTL to prefer-region so we can quickly shift back after warmup. Also set autoscaler buffer to +20% for the 30m after each cohort.

maria: Will update runbook and add step to post a short status message in #status and notify Dedicated customers via the support ticketing broadcast. Anyone object to the timing?

chris: Fine from CS side. I'll prepare the outbound message and a canned response for tickets.

priya: Budget OK for the one-off backfill egress. Please add line item to the ops spend tracker.

devon: Oncall will be watching p50/p95/p99 + queue length. If we see sustained queue growth >20% for 15m we escalate.

maria: Thanks all — I'll post the finalized runbook and the small customer blurb in here after the rehearse. Checklist done: canary -> validate -> cohort-by-cohort drains -> warmup -> confirm metrics. :white_check_mark: 

sam: dropping link to runbook draft: https://redwood.internal.runbooks/infra/eu-west3-maint-2026 (will update)

maria: linking patch playbook and KV warmup scripts in the runbook.

infra-bot: reminder: oncall rotation @devon starts 2026-03-21T00:00Z.
